newsitem.title: FRANCE: SNCF studies Eurotunnel claim options.
newsitem.headline: SNCF studies Eurotunnel claim options.

text.p: SNCF, the French railway operator, is looking at the possibility of claiming lost revenues from Eurotunnel SA/Plc, and SNCF spokesman said on Monday.

"The SNCF is suffering a commercial prejudice as it is unable to operate the Eurostar," the spokesman said. "Naturally it expects to be compensated and is currently studying the possibilities open to it."
The Eurostar passenger service through the Channel Tunnel has been suspended since a fire in the tunnel a week ago.
The SNCF deplored a decision last Thursday by the Franco-British safety commission to allow only freight service through the tunnel.
The SNCF spokesman could not estimate the losses or the size of any claim against Eurotunnel other than to say the amounts ran into "several million francs per day."
However, some 19,000 Eurostar tickets were being sold daily since the beginning of November, he added.

Eurotunnel is insured for operating losses with French insurer UAP. Daily newspaper Le Monde said on Monday the insurance covers revenues based on only the first half and does not take into account the rise since.
A UAP executive told Reuters that in general it is possible to insure for "anticipated revenues when the market is growing."
Le Monde reported the insurance does not cover the minimum usage fee that Eurotunnel receives from the railway companies for booking half the Tunnel capacity.
The UAP spokesman said it was too early to put any figures to any Eurotunnel claim as the company and UAP are still in the process of evaluating the damage from last week's fire.
"The process will take several days or weeks," he said.
A second SNCF official said the operator has to agree any claim with its British and Belgian counterparts after detailed studies by the legal departments.
